entries.title: Watermill Fantasy Puppy Rescue
entries.description: A highly detailed prompt for a cinematic live-action fantasy sequence at a riverside watermill involving a horned man protecting his puppy from a basilisk.
entries.prompt:
FORMAT
20 seconds, horizontal 16:9. A cinematic live-action fantasy sequence at an old riverside watermill. A horned young man protects his puppy during an ambush. When he falls, the puppy returns the favor. Fast physical action at real speed, followed by a quiet ending. No dialogue, captions or titles.

PHOTO REFERENCES
image1 defines the young man. Match his face, complexion, hair, ears, both horns and their individual colors, costume, belt, accessories and boots. Preserve the placement of each horn relative to his own head.

image2 shows the same three-eyed Dalmatian in two forms. The small dog on the left is the puppy seen at the beginning and end. The giant dog on the right is its transformed body. Match the build, face, coat, ears, paws and three-eye arrangement of each form. The central forehead eye glows blue immediately before the first transformation. Only one dog exists in the scene.

CINEMATIC LOOK
Make this feel like a finished scene from a big-budget live-action fantasy film. A real actor photographed on a weathered mill set. The creatures share his light, lens perspective, contact shadows and interaction with the ground. Horizontal cinema composition, natural 24 fps movement, fine restrained grain, soft highlight roll-off and believable motion blur. Use a moderately wide 32 mm perspective for the action. Keep the relevant feet, contact points and landing surfaces readable. Move closer for the ending.

Late dusk. Cool skylight reflected off the river illuminates the wet landing. A warm oil lantern beside the mill doorway grazes the young man's face, hair and costume. The dark mill wall separates the pale fur from the background. Show damp wood fibers, dull iron nails, droplets caught in fur and grit pressed into the grooves of the basilisk's armor. The blue flame briefly lights nearby skin, stone and scales. Preserve detail in the white fur. Camera movement follows the actors with the weight of a human-operated cinema camera. Use a brief reactive movement at the plank rupture, then hold steady enough to read the fight.

SET AND BLOCKING
A short wooden walkway approaches a broad stone loading platform from upstream. The river runs along one side of the platform. The mill wall runs parallel to it on the opposite side. A recessed doorway opens near the upstream end of the wall. A waterwheel turns several meters downstream, beyond the platform.

The platform is wide enough for the transformed dog to land, plant all four paws and push. During the fight the puppy starts at the doorway, the basilisk is near the middle, and the boy falls farther downstream beside the wall. This leaves an open lane from the doorway across the basilisk's flank toward the river. Establish these positions visually before the puppy jumps. Maintain screen direction across cuts.

BASILISK
A heavy, six-legged reptile roughly the length of a large crocodile. Broad wedge-shaped skull, low belly, muscular tail, overlapping dark armor plates. Its six legs support its weight. Its torso and hips bend as it turns. Wet claws find purchase on rough stone and slip where the surface is smooth. The giant Dalmatian is tall enough to place a shoulder beneath the raised side rim of its armor.

TIMELINE

0.0-3.5 | Something under the boards
Begin with the boy and puppy already on the final section of the walkway, one step from the stone platform. Frame them together. The puppy flinches at a metallic tick. A nail jumps beside its paw and the board directly behind it buckles upward. The boy immediately scoops up the puppy and bounds onto the stone. As his boots land, the basilisk's skull bursts through the boards they just left. Capture the escape and eruption in the same moving shot. Broken timber drops into the current. The doorway is within arm's reach.

3.5-7.5 | One bite, one tail strike
The boy sets the puppy in the doorway recess. The basilisk hauls itself onto the upstream end of the platform and lunges toward him. He dodges downstream along the wall. The jaws snap shut behind his shoulder. The creature pivots to follow him. Its hips rotate and its trailing tail sweeps low, catching him once behind the ankles. Show the tail contact and his fall together. He lands on his side beside the wall, downstream of the doorway.

The basilisk finishes its turn with its head pointing downstream toward the fallen boy. Its body is roughly parallel to the river, several meters from the drop. Its landward flank now faces the puppy. For a brief beat, show all three positions: the puppy at the doorway, the basilisk side-on ahead of it, and the boy clear of the puppy's attack line.

7.5-10.0 | The puppy transforms in the leap
One continuous lateral three-quarter shot through takeoff, transformation, contact and landing. The puppy's central eye flashes blue. Two quick strides out of the doorway. Its hind paws push off the stone while it is still visibly small. Frame its airborne silhouette against the lighter river beyond the platform.

Immediately after takeoff, tight blue flame races from its forehead down its back. In less than half a second its chest expands, legs thicken and paws broaden into the giant form from image2. The flame follows the contours of the growing body so the audience sees the transformation itself. Its center of mass keeps moving forward along one uninterrupted arc. It reaches full size before contact.

Both forepaws strike the basilisk's landward shoulder together in one impact. The blow knocks the jaws sideways, away from the boy. The dog's forepaws come off the armor and meet the stone, followed by its hind paws. Its elbows and hocks flex under its weight. The basilisk staggers toward the river but remains on the platform. The dog lands on the landward side with stone still ahead of it. No cut or slow motion during the leap.

10.0-15.0 | The shove into the river
The basilisk spreads its legs to regain traction. The dog is already standing against its exposed flank. It lowers one shoulder beneath the side armor, spreads its hind paws and drives forward. This second action is a sustained push from the ground. Show the hind legs working, the basilisk's claws dragging and the distance to the edge closing.

The basilisk's river-side feet slip over the lip. Its heavy torso tips sideways and the remaining claws tear free. As its weight goes over, the dog breaks contact and braces on the stone. Hold wide enough to see the dog stop on the bank as the basilisk hits the river below. Water splashes up over the dog's chest. The current pulls the armored back downstream past the wheel. The boy stays on the ground beside the wall throughout the shove.

15.0-20.0 | The hand on its head
As the splash falls, the boy pushes himself into a seated position against the wall. The giant dog turns and crosses the short distance back to him. It lowers its head into his waiting palm.

Move into a medium two-shot at the seated boy's height. His hand rests between the dog's ears. A low blue flame travels down its back as its body smoothly contracts into the original puppy. His hand follows its head down. Tilt gently with the movement, keeping the changing head size and his fingers visible together. Once small, the puppy shakes the river droplets from its coat. The boy blinks as the spray hits his face, then smiles. End on that reaction.

AUDIO AND CONTINUITY
Establish running water and the uneven wooden knock of the wheel. Let the small metallic nail tick precede the loud plank rupture. Give each physical event a distinct sound: snapping jaws, the low tail sweep, boots scraping stone, the brief rush of blue flame, one heavy landing, claws grinding across the platform, then the splash. Let the wheel and close breathing return in the final moment.

The walkway remains broken. The boy stays down until the basilisk falls into the river. The puppy leaves the doorway once. The dog remains g

entries.prompt:
晩秋の晴れた朝、山あいの渓谷。旅の途中のさくらが1人で吊り橋を渡っている。手前の岸の錆びた留め金具で、割りピンが折れ、太いピンが弾け飛ぶ。右のワイヤーが外れて宙へ跳ね、右側の吊りワイヤーが順に切れていく。床板が次々に谷へ落ち、さくらの足が穴を踏み外す。

そこへ山道から男が駆けつける。2人が同時に手をかざすと、落ちかけた板が宙で止まる。「こっちは持つ。……来い」。「……その声」。さくらは傾いた橋を伝って岸へ戻り、2人で橋を水平に戻す。「どうして、ここに？」「浜から、ついてきた。あんたが、俺みたいに全部忘れる前に。……もう使うな」。「……名前は？」「……ナギ。そう呼ばれてる」。言われたそばから、さくらは力でワイヤーを岩に結び直す。「……言ったそばから」。男は山道を去る。「あの人……なんて、名乗ったっけ」。

一緒に旅をしている友達が手持ちで撮った記録。BGMなし。光やオーラは足さず、橋とワイヤーと板が動くだけにした。崩れるのは最初から最後まで橋の右側だけ。男の顔は一度も映していない。崩れの場面は、ピン・ワイヤー・床板の順に壊れていく絵コンテを描いてから撃った。締めの「わすれたもの」帳と「つづく」だけコードで描いた。
entries.translated_prompt:
On a sunny morning in late autumn, in a mountain valley. Sakura, on a journey, crosses a suspension bridge alone. At the rusty fasteners on the near shore, split pins break and thick pins fly off. The right wire detaches and jumps into the air, and the right suspension wires snap one by one. Floorboards fall into the valley one after another, and Sakura's feet miss the holes.

A man rushes down from the mountain path. When they both raise their hands simultaneously, the falling boards stop in mid-air. "I'll hold this side. ...Come." "...That voice." Sakura returns to the shore along the tilted bridge, and together they restore the bridge to horizontal. "Why are you here?" "Followed you from the beach. Before you forget everything like me. ...Don't use it anymore." "...What's your name?" "...Nagi. That's what I'm called." Immediately after being told, Sakura uses force to retie the wire to the rock. "...Right after saying that." The man leaves down the mountain path. "That person... what did he call himself?"

Recorded handheld by a friend traveling together. No BGM. No added light or aura, only moving bridge, wires, and boards. Collapse happens only on the right side of the bridge throughout. Never show the man's face. For the collapse scene, drew storyboards breaking in order of pin-wire-floorboard before shooting. Only drew the closing 'Forgotten Things' ledger and 'To be continued' with code.

entries.title: Western Comedy Pig Rider Scene
entries.description: A highly detailed prompt for a western comedy scene involving a man riding a pig, referencing image inputs for character consistency.
entries.prompt:
15 seconds. Horizontal 16:9. Photorealistic live-action western comedy scene, shot like a big-budget Hollywood film. Real-time speed, natural physics, no slow motion.

REFERENCES
Image Reference 1: the photo of the man riding the pig. Defines the exact appearance of both: his face, chestnut-brown bowl haircut with straight bangs, thick dark handlebar mustache, heavily muscular build, open short-sleeve cream-and-black cow-spot shirt over a white tank top with a printed hot dog graphic, wide brown leather belt with a round brass star buckle, dark brown worn leather trousers, brown tooled leather cowboy boots, gold wristwatch. The pig: large black-and-pink spotted pig with coarse bristly hair, brown leather aviator cap with cream sheepskin trim, round brass-framed goggles with dark lenses, black paisley bandana, tooled brown leather western saddle with a saddle horn and brass buckles, leather reins. Match the reference in every shot. Ignore its grey studio background.

REALISM
Real actors, a real trained pig, a physical ranch location. Natural skin with pores and sweat, dust on boots and clothes, worn leather, weathered wood with cracks and splinters, frayed rope fibres. The pig has real weight, about 150 kg. Everything that carries it bends, creaks and strains believably. No cartoon look, plastic skin or game-engine appearance.

CHARACTERS
Pigboy: the man from Image Reference 1. Stern, calm, never smiles, completely confident. Seated on the pig, his seat is about 1 metre above the ground and his head about 1.8 metres.
Three ranch cowboys, all in their 30s-40s, sun-tanned, sweaty, in dusty felt cowboy hats, faded cotton work shirts with rolled sleeves, suspenders, canvas trousers, worn leather boots.
- Cowboy 1: the biggest, broad shoulders, thick brown beard, tan hat. Cocky.
- Cowboy 2: lean, blond stubble, grey hat. Struggling.
- Cowboy 3: stocky, black mustache, black hat. Struggling.

ENVIRONMENT
A dusty western ranch yard at midday. Dry packed dirt, small dust clouds at every step. The pull-up bar is an old hitching post: TWO thick sun-blackened wooden posts set firmly in the ground 3 metres apart, joined by ONE horizontal round log rail 2.3 metres above the ground, about 12 cm thick, its middle wrapped with frayed hemp rope where hands grip. Iron rings for tying horses hang from the posts. Beside it: a wooden water barrel and a split-rail fence with saddles hanging on it. Background: a weathered barn, a windmill, dry hills, a pale blue sky. Hard midday sun from above-left, short sharp shadows, natural warm tones, dust floating in the air.

TIMELINE

00:00-00:02 | HOOK - THE RIDER
First frame already in motion. Side tracking shot at the rider's eye level, camera moving alongside. Pigboy rides the pig at a steady trot from left to right across the dusty yard, shown in profile, reins in one hand, bangs bouncing, stern face. Hooves kick up dirt. Ahead of him, about 20 metres away on the right side of the frame, the hitching post with the three cowboys hanging from it is clearly visible in soft focus. Cut after a completed stride.

00:02-00:05 | THE COWBOYS
Medium-wide front three-quarter shot of the hitching post. All three cowboys hang from the log rail side by side, feet off the ground, knees slightly bent. Cowboy 1 pulls himself up until his chin clears the log, lowers down, lets go, drops 30 cm and lands on both boots with a puff of dust, grinning at the others. Cowboy 2 and Cowboy 3 still hang with trembling arms, red faces and gritted teeth; Cowboy 2 manages only half a pull-up and sinks back down.

00:05-00:08 | THE ARRIVAL
Hoof steps and a grunt are heard. Cowboy 2 and Cowboy 3 drop from the rail onto their boots, and all three cowboys turn and step aside. The pig trots into frame from the left and stops one step in front of the log rail, facing it, Pigboy upright in the saddle. Only after the pig has stopped, Pigboy looks at the cowboys with quiet contempt and says in a low, calm voice: "Let me show you how it's done."

00:08-00:12 | THE PULL-UP
One continuous medium-wide front three-quarter shot, no cuts, showing the log rail, both his hands, his face, the whole pig and its hooves. The pig takes one step forward between the two posts, its body perpendicular to the log rail, and stops so the rail runs just in front of Pigboy's face. The pig's head passes under the rail with plenty of clearance.
Still seated, Pigboy raises both arms and grips the rope-wrapped log with both hands, arms fully extended. His boots are locked in the stirrups, his thighs clamp the pig's sides, the saddle girth is cinched tight under the pig's belly.
He pulls up in one slow, powerful movement: back and arm muscles flex, veins show. The pig rises together with him as ONE unit through the saddle: all four hooves leave the ground and lift 55 cm into the air, the pig's legs dangle and paddle calmly, its belly hangs from the tight girth. His chin rises just above the log, in front of it. The log bends slightly and creaks, both posts flex, dust drops from the wood, the rope fibres strain.
He holds at the top for one second, then lowers smoothly. The pig's hooves touch the dirt softly, front pair then back pair. He releases the log and rests both hands on the saddle horn.

00:12-00:13.5 | CALM
Medium close-up of Pigboy, still seated, not even breathing hard. He runs one hand over his bowl haircut to fix his bangs.

00:13.5-00:15 | THE PUNCHLINE
Medium-wide shot: Pigboy on the pig under the hitching post, the three stunned cowboys standing beside them in silence. Cowboy 1 slowly takes off his hat and holds it against his chest. The pig snorts and shakes its head once. End on that snort.

CAMERA
Cinematic handheld coverage with motivated cuts after completed movements. Shots of 1.5-3 seconds, except the pull-up, which is one continuous shot. The pig always moves left to right on screen. Slight hand shake, faint film grain, natural motion blur. Camera and crew never appear in frame.

AUDIO & DIALOGUE
Natural sound only: dry wind, a distant windmill creaking, hooves thudding on packed dirt, pig grunts, the cowboys' heavy breathing and strained groans, boots landing in dust, wood creaking under load, rope fibres straining. The only spoken line, by Pigboy, in English: "Let me show you how it's done." Final pig snort. No music, narration or laugh track.

CONTINUITY
Pigboy never leaves the saddle at any moment. The pig rises only while he is pulling up and only through the saddle connection; it never floats on its own. The hitching post stays in place, bends slightly under load but never breaks. Cowboys who dropped from the rail stay on the ground. Exactly three cowboys throughout. Same sun, same yard, same background in every shot. Preserve his face, bowl haircut, mustache, cow-print shirt, hot dog tank top, brass star buckle, leather trousers and cowboy boots, and the pig's aviator cap, goggles, bandana and saddle throughout.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS
No floating, teleportation, duplicated people or animals, extra limbs, changing outfits, breaking bar, rider standing in the stirrups, rider dismounting, pig's head hitting the rail, slow motion, cartoon style, CGI look, captions, subtitles, text, watermarks.

entries.prompt:
TITLE: THE ELEVATOR – FLOOR 0

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic Korean cinematic mystery thriller with the visual quality of a premium Korean feature film.

CHARACTER:
A 28-year-old Korean businessman with short black hair, wearing a black formal suit, white shirt, and black tie. Maintain identical facial features, clothing, and appearance throughout every scene.

SCENE 1 (0–7 SECONDS):
Late at night in Seoul, a businessman enters a luxurious modern apartment elevator. He presses floor 18. The elevator doors slowly close. He checks his wristwatch. The elevator begins moving upward.

SCENE 2 (7–14 SECONDS):
Suddenly, the elevator lights flicker. The floor display changes from 12 to 11, then displays an unfamiliar number: 0. The elevator stops. The doors slowly open, revealing a long, completely empty underground corridor with cold fluorescent lighting.

SCENE 3 (14–22 SECONDS):
The businessman looks confused and steps slightly forward. At the far end of the corridor, he notices a little Korean girl wearing a red coat. She is standing completely still, facing away from him. He calls out, but she does not respond. Suddenly, the elevator doors begin closing behind him.

SCENE 4 (22–30 SECONDS):
He rushes back into the elevator and presses the emergency button. The doors close. He looks into the elevator mirror and sees the little girl standing directly behind him. He turns around immediately. Nobody is there.

The elevator display changes to FLOOR 18.

FINAL SHOT:
As the doors open, the businessman sees himself standing outside the elevator, wearing the exact same suit, staring directly at him with a terrifying smile.

CUT TO BLACK.

CINEMATOGRAPHY:
Premium Korean thriller cinematography, realistic human expressions, atmospheric shadows, slow camera pushes, cinematic close-ups, symmetrical framing, natural skin textures, realistic elevator reflections, professional color grading, and subtle film grain.

SOUND DESIGN:
Elevator mechanical hum, soft electrical buzzing, footsteps echoing through the corridor, subtle heartbeat sound, suspenseful cinematic music, and sudden silence during the final reveal.

STRICT REQUIREMENTS:
Photorealistic live-action only. No animation, no cartoon style, no artificial-looking characters, no inconsistent faces, no random wardrobe changes, no unnecessary dialogue, no watermarks. Preserve character continuity and realistic physical movement throughout the entire 30-second film.

entries.prompt:
Create an exactly 30-second photorealistic cinematic sad relationship video for Facebook Reels, vertical 9:16.

CHARACTER CONSISTENCY:
Husband: 33-year-old man with short black hair, wearing a charcoal-grey shirt and black trousers. Emotionally distant, tired eyes, rarely smiles.
Wife: 29-year-old woman with long dark hair, wearing a simple cream-colored dress. Gentle eyes, loving expression, visibly hurt but trying to stay strong.

Maintain identical faces, hairstyles, clothing, voices, and body proportions throughout.

SETTING: A modest, beautifully arranged dining room at night. A homemade dinner, two plates, candles, and a wedding photograph on the wall.

SCENE 1 — WAITING (0–7 seconds)
Start immediately with the wife looking at the clock. She carefully adjusts the dinner plates and lights a small candle. She looks toward the door.

Wife whispers: "I hope he likes what I made tonight."

Camera: Close-up of her hopeful eyes, followed by the untouched second plate.

Sound: Slow, sad piano begins.

SCENE 2 — HIS ARRIVAL (7–14 seconds)
The husband enters, puts his keys on the table, and walks past her without smiling.

Wife: "You're home. I made your favorite dinner."

Husband, looking at his phone: "I already ate. I'm tired."

Her smile slowly disappears.

Camera: Close-up of her face as she quietly looks down.

SCENE 3 — HER LAST EFFORT (14–22 seconds)
She follows him a few steps and gently asks:

Wife: "Can we at least sit together for ten minutes?"

Husband: "Please don't start. I just want some peace."

He walks into the bedroom.

The wife stands silently. Her eyes fill with tears, but she does not call him back.

SCENE 4 — THE ENDING (22–30 seconds)
Camera: Slow close-up of the wife sitting alone at the dining table. She removes the untouched second plate and looks at the wedding photograph.

Wife whispers: "I cooked with love. I guess you weren't hungry for it."

A tear rolls down her cheek. She blows out the candle.

End on the empty chair opposite her.

AUDIO: Continuous melancholic piano and soft strings, natural room ambience, clear emotional dialogue.

VISUAL STYLE: Photorealistic cinematic acting, subtle tears, realistic expressions, warm candlelight contrasting with the cold dark room, slow camera movements, natural lip-sync. No extra characters, subtitles, text overlays, cartoon effects, or abrupt cuts. The story must begin at second 1 and finish at second 30.

entries.title: Knight House Party Camcorder
entries.description: A creative prompt for a DV camcorder style video featuring a knight in armor partying in a house.
entries.prompt:
DV 16mm tape camcorder handheld feel. Hand shake, misaligned framing, delayed focus pulls, clumsy zooms, occasional face cut-off framing, imperfect shots. Camcorder and camera operator never appear on screen.

20 seconds, horizontal 16:9. A friend's highlight tape from a house party already at its peak. Packed wall to wall with adult guests. Shoot at shoulder height inside the crowd. Red cups, open cans, bottles, beer dripping off the table. People dance behind the action and arms keep crossing the lens. On-camera light blows out nearby faces, the far side of the room falls into warm shadow. Real-time speed. Cut into actions already underway and out on impact.

Same knight throughout: closed black great helm, dark armor, black cape, brushed silver breastplate. Paint the complete logo from Image1 across his chest: black square with its white M, followed by the exact MakeUGC wordmark. The logo turns with his torso.

0–2s | Start inside the packed living room, shooting across a beer-pong table. Behind a woman mid-sip, the knight smashes shoulder-first through the drywall toward the camera, bottle raised. Plaster bursts outward. The guests recoil to either side, clearing the view. As he steps through, his silver chest faces the camcorder light for half a second: the complete logo from Image1 is clearly readable, white M in its black square and the MakeUGC wordmark beside it. His steel boot lands on the table. Red cups jump. Cut on impact.

2–4s | Cut to table level. Boots pound a sturdy low wooden party table to the bass. Half-full cups bounce, beer jumps over their rims. A friend at the edge sprays champagne overhead. Whip up from the boots into the next shot.

4–7s | Hold a single front-on shot for the joke. The knight kneels beside the near edge of the low table, visor facing the lens. Two big, plus-size adult women are dancing on the tabletop, one in red jeans on his left, one in blue jeans on his right. They face opposite ends of the table, their backsides toward the helmet between them. On the same bass hit both take one step backward and squeeze the sides of his helmet between their backsides. One beat of visible contact. CLANG. They bounce apart laughing. He raises his cup in a deadpan toast. The crowd loses it. Cut on the cheer.

7–10s | Close on a penguin in an orange life vest. Snap wide: roof shingles under its feet, the knight beside it, a turquoise pool far below and partygoers lining both sides. The penguin launches off the roof of the two-story house. The knight takes a running jump after it, cape flipping up. Whip down from the roof edge: small splash, huge splash, the front row gets soaked.

10–13s | Hard cut wide. A real elephant shoulders through the living room with the wet knight riding behind its ears. Guests scramble onto sofas with their drinks overhead. Cut to table height as the trunk sweeps a whole row of beer-pong cups toward the lens. The rider grabs on as the elephant turns.

13–15.5s | A crowd pours out onto the porch, chanting and passing a bottle over their heads. The wet knight gets shoved sideways against the white rail. The camera swings after him and catches a rust-red prop launcher on the boards by his boot.

entries.title: Korean Zombie Rooftop Chase
entries.description: A detailed prompt for an intense Korean zombie action sequence featuring a rooftop chase and acrobatics.
entries.prompt:
Create an extremely intense, ultra-realistic 30-second cinematic Korean zombie action sequence.
Recreate the dramatic nighttime rooftop setting, elevated metal scaffolding, dangerous acrobatic movements, zombie attacks, emotional close-ups, and desperate rooftop escape.

The entire sequence must feel like a high-budget Korean action movie, featuring realistic human physics, breathtaking stunt choreography, seamless camera tracking, terrifying zombie performances, and explosive cinematic sound design.
MAIN FEMALE CHARACTER — IDENTITY AND APPEARANCE

A beautiful, athletic Korean woman with a short, chin-length pastel pink bob haircut, soft feathered layers, a side part, and naturally flowing hair.
Her pastel pink hair must remain clearly visible throughout the entire video, even in dark nighttime lighting.
Individual strands move realistically during running, jumping, falling, and fighting.
Her face is expressive, with intense eyes, natural skin texture, light sweat, and a determined survival instinct.

Character Consistency:

Maintain identical facial features, pastel pink hair color, haircut, clothing, body proportions, and footwear across every shot.

ENVIRONMENT

A massive residential apartment complex at night, surrounded by tall concrete buildings.

A narrow temporary metal scaffolding bridge connects two rooftops high above the ground.

Dozens of infected zombies are chasing the protagonist through the scaffolding.

The platform vibrates violently beneath their footsteps.

Her pastel pink hair whips backward as she runs at full speed, breathing heavily.

Camera: Fast backward tracking shot transitioning into a dynamic side profile. Slight handheld shake.

Sound: Rapid footsteps on metal, zombie screams, heavy breathing, distant explosions.

SCENE 02 — THE IMPOSSIBLE FLIP (0:04–0:08)

The woman reaches a vertical scaffolding support pole as zombies close in.

Without stopping, she grabs the metal pole with both hands, swings her body upward, and performs a spectacular inverted acrobatic rotation.

Her legs extend high into the air while her torso twists around the pole.

Her pastel pink hair falls toward the ground due to gravity.

A zombie lunges beneath her, narrowly missing her body.

Camera: Dramatic low-angle tracking shot following the complete rotation, with a brief slow-motion moment at the highest point.

Physics: Realistic momentum, believable grip strength, natural hair movement, and accurate body mechanics.

SCENE 03 — THE METAL WALKWAY (0:08–0:12)

She releases the pole and lands on the narrow scaffolding walkway.

Immediately, she sprints toward the camera as several zombies emerge behind her.

Her expression shifts from determination to panic when she notices the walkway ending ahead.

The metal structure rattles under the approaching horde.

Camera: Rapid dolly backward, close-up of her face, followed by an overhead view revealing the enormous drop beneath the platform.

SCENE 04 — THE LAST HAND (0:12–0:17)

A terrifying infected woman suddenly grabs the protagonist's wrist near the edge of the scaffolding.

The pastel-pink-haired woman loses her balance and drops onto the metal walkway.

The infected woman leans over her, gripping her arm tightly.

Extreme Close-Up:

The protagonist's frightened eyes, trembling lips, sweat-covered skin, and strands of pastel pink hair falling across her face.

The zombie's gray, damaged skin, dark veins, and unnatural eyes are visible inches from her face.

The protagonist desperately twists her body and pulls her arm free.

Camera: Tight handheld close-ups alternating between their faces and hands.

SCENE 05 — THE HORDE BREAKS THROUGH (0:17–0:21)

More zombies suddenly burst onto the scaffolding.

The woman scrambles to her feet as infected bodies collide with the metal railings.

She ducks beneath a lunging zombie, spins around a support beam, and pushes herself toward the edge.

The scaffolding shakes violently.

A section of the metal railing collapses behind her.

Camera: Fast lateral tracking, whip pans, aggressive close-ups, and a wide shot revealing the enormous zombie crowd.

Sound: Metal crashing, frantic footsteps, terrifying screams, escalating orchestral percussion.

SCENE 06 — THE ROOFTOP LEAP (0:21–0:26)

The woman reaches the very end of the scaffolding.

Across a dangerous gap lies the rooftop of another apartment building.

She looks down for a fraction of a second, then accelerates into one final sprint.

With a powerful push from her right foot, she launches herself across the gap.

Her body stretches through the air, arms extended forward, legs trailing behind.

Her pastel pink hair flies dramatically in the wind.

Camera: Epic side-profile wide shot showing her airborne between two rooftops, followed by a dynamic tracking camera moving alongside her.

Use a brief cinematic slow-motion effect during the peak of the jump.

SCENE 07 — SURVIVAL (0:26–0:30)

She reaches the opposite rooftop and lands hard, stumbling forward before catching herself.

She immediately turns around.

Behind her, dozens of zombies gather at the broken scaffolding edge, reaching toward her across the gap.

Close-up of her face as she gasps for air.

Her pastel pink hair is disheveled, her face covered in sweat, and her eyes widen with fear.

Suddenly, a terrifying zombie scream echoes from somewhere behind her on the new rooftop.

She freezes.

Camera: Slowly pushes toward her shocked expression.

Final Shot: Hard cut to black.

CINEMATOGRAPHY AND TECHNICAL DIRECTION

Use physically realistic action choreography, cinematic 35mm and 50mm lens compositions, dramatic high-angle shots, intense handheld tracking, realistic motion blur, and selective slow motion during major acrobatic movements.

Maintain consistent rooftop geography and believable distances between buildings.

The character's movements must connect naturally between shots.

Color Grade:

Cold steel-blue nighttime shadows, muted gray concrete, subtle orange firelight, and the protagonist's distinctive pastel pink hair.

MUSIC AND SOUND DESIGN

Aggressive cinematic percussion, metallic impacts, rapid breathing, zombie growls, distant sirens, wind, and a dramatic bass impact during the final jump.

The soundtrack must intensify throughout the rooftop chase, become terrifyingly intimate during the infected woman's attack, and reach its maximum intensity during the final rooftop leap.

End with a sudden zombie scream followed by complete silence and a hard cut to black.

entries.title: Old Québec Christmas FPV Vlog
entries.description: A detailed prompt for a continuous FPV shot through Old Québec during winter, focusing on specific camera movements, lighting, and festive elements like carolers and snow.
entries.prompt:
One CONTINUOUS FPV shot, no cuts, one unbroken take, at a relaxed, curious cruising pace — like a traveler's handheld vlog drifting through the city, gentle natural sway and micro-shake, never rushed. The footage NEVER reverses. NO slow motion except one half-second beat at the reveal. Photoreal framing. GHOST CAMERA: only the CAMERA moves — INVISIBLE, no drone, selfie stick, hands or reflection ever appear in frame. The camera only ever DESCENDS or travels level, never climbs. NEVER a straight line: it weaves in soft left-right curves, turning to look at whatever catches its eye. NO fade to black — the take runs until time runs out, still immersed in the city.

CINEMATIC CAPTURE: ultra-wide 14mm lens, natural motion blur, fine grain, lens flares off streetlights. Blue-hour winter in Old Québec: fresh snow on every roof, warm gold windows, strings of white lights, steam curling from chimneys and doorways. Grade: icy blue and copper green against warm amber — a premium winter travel vlog, NOT a game engine, NOT animation.

The shot opens from the provided start frame, high above Old Québec in falling snow, the Château Frontenac on its clifftop on the RIGHT, the frozen ice-floe river and Lower Town below on the LEFT. The camera glides down past the château's copper turrets, icicles glinting along the eaves, and settles onto the Dufferin Terrace, drifting along the boardwalk in easy curves. Life is everywhere, close: a horse-drawn calèche clops past under a red blanket, the horse snorting steam, the driver tipping his fur hat; two kids SHRIEK down the long wooden toboggan slide on a sled, kicking up powder right beside the lens; a violinist in a toque plays under a gazebo. The camera eases over the railing and descends the cliff beside the funicular as its red car slides down, then drifts into Rue du Petit-Champlain at walking-plus speed, weaving gently between shoppers: a woman holding a steaming paper cup, laughing with a friend; a shopkeeper hanging a wreath on her door. THE ONE CLOSE MOMENT: at ARM'S LENGTH, a little girl in red mittens on her father's shoulders throws back her head catching snowflakes on her tongue — the camera lingers a beat, then moves on. A vendor pours hot maple syrup in lines onto fresh snow, kids rolling the golden taffy onto sticks. The lane opens out. THE REVEAL: half-second slow motion — the stone square of Place Royale opening up, the old stone church glowing amber, a giant fir tree blazing with lights, carolers in scarves mid-song, snowflakes hanging motionless in the warm light — then back to the relaxed glide as the snowfall THICKENS into soft gold-lit flakes; the camera circles the tree past the carolers, slips through a stone archway onto the riverfront and cruises low along the edge.

entries.title: Toddler in Inflatable Candy World
entries.description: A detailed cinematic prompt for Seedance 2.5 to generate a 15-second live-action short film of a Korean toddler playing in a soft, inflatable candy-themed playground.
entries.prompt:
A 15-second live-action cinematic short film, 16:9, 24 fps, realistic 4K film quality. Bright, soft daylight inside a giant inflatable candy world playground. Everything is soft, bouncy, and candy-themed: giant inflatable lollipops, gummy bears, candy canes, marshmallow platforms, chocolate bar ramps, and colorful bounce surfaces. No hard concrete, no sharp edges, no high drops. All surfaces are soft vinyl and air-filled.

The entire play area is one continuous soft inflatable structure with low, rounded obstacles. Every action stays low to the ground or on gentle soft slopes. No dangerous heights, no hard landings, no risk of falling far.

【Core Contrast】
The protagonist is a very small Korean toddler boy (around 1.5 years old) in a white long-sleeve shirt and colorful shorts. He moves with genuine toddler energy — wobbly, bouncy, short steps, lots of balancing with his arms out, curious, and a bit clumsy. He is not athletic or skilled. He simply explores and plays with high energy the way a real toddler would.

【Character Lock】
The protagonist is a cute 1.5-year-old Korean toddler boy with short black buzz-cut hair, round chubby face, big dark eyes, small nose, fair skin, and soft baby features. He wears a loose white long-sleeve shirt with an open collar and a necktie, colorful bright short pants (rainbow/floral pattern), white socks, and white sneakers. 

His outfit, hair, and face stay completely consistent across all shots. He never looks at the camera or poses. His expression is focused and curious, mouth slightly open.

Objective: Bounce and crawl through the inflatable candy course and press the big soft red candy button at the end.

【Safe Spatial Layout】
All obstacles are soft inflatables:
- Starting area: soft marshmallow platform
- Low inflatable candy cane (about knee-high for him)
- Soft gummy bear bounce mound
- Gentle inflatable slide ramp
- Low soft chocolate bar barrier
- Finish: big soft red button on an inflatable wall

Everything is low, soft, and bouncy. Continuous soft flooring is always visible.

【Camera Rules】
Use six clearly paced shots alternating between close rear-follow, first-person POV, side view, and low tracking. Wide-angle lenses (17–24mm) with natural distortion. Subject stays near the center of frame. Soft, bouncy camera movement that matches the inflatable surfaces.

【Absolute First-Person POV Rules】
Clean first-person POV from a toddler’s eye level. Never show any part of the boy’s face, hair, or body outline. Only his small hands, forearms, and occasionally his shoes or knees may appear at the bottom of the frame.

【Shot One | 0–2 Seconds | Close Rear Follow】
Low tracking shot behind him. He is already doing a wobbly toddler run across a soft marshmallow platform, arms slightly out for balance. Short, choppy steps. His white shirt and colorful shorts bounce with him. He reaches a gentle soft slope and carefully steps down it with both feet, one step at a time, slightly unsteady.

【Shot Two | 2–4 Seconds | First-Person POV】
Clean toddler eye-level POV. A soft low inflatable candy cane is ahead. His small hands reach forward and press on top of it. He tries to climb/step over it with a wobbly motion, one leg lifting high, body leaning, then lands softly on the other side with a little bounce. Hands and shoes briefly visible at the bottom of frame.

【Shot Three | 4–6.3 Seconds | Side View Bounce】
Side tracking shot. He runs toward a soft gummy bear bounce mound. He steps onto it and bounces once or twice with both feet, arms flailing slightly for balance, then continues forward. Very toddler-like, not a controlled jump.

【Shot Four | 6.3–8.3 Seconds | Front Follow Down Soft Ramp】
Low front tracking shot moving backward. He carefully walks down a gentle inflatable slide ramp, both hands out for balance, taking small steps. At the bottom he lowers his body and crawls under a low soft chocolate bar obstacle on his hands and knees.

【Shot Five | 8.3–11.6 Seconds | Main Soft Wall Climb】
Third-person shot. He approaches a low soft inflatable barrier (about his chest height). He places both hands on top and tries to climb over it with a wobbly toddler climb — one knee up, body rocking, then he pulls himself over and lands softly on the other side with a little bounce and a small recovery step. Not a vault. Just a clumsy but determined climb.

【Shot Six | 11.6–15 Seconds | Final Approach & Button】
Low tracking shot from behind. He does a short bouncy run between giant soft candy obstacles, arms out for balance. He reaches the big soft red button and presses it with both hands. The button makes a soft candy-like ding. He stops, puts his hands on his knees, and breathes heavily with a focused, slightly tired toddler expression. Cut to black.

【Character Performance】
All movement must look like a real 1.5-year-old: short steps, high cadence but unstable, arms out for balance, occasional small stumbles that he recovers from, curious head movements, natural blinking. No athletic skill, no smooth parkour, no heroic poses. Pure toddler energy.

【Background Music】
Bright, playful 140–150 BPM music with a light music-box / xylophone melody mixed with soft bouncy electronic beats. Music syncs with his steps and the soft bounces. No heavy industrial sounds. Action sounds (soft footfalls, bounces, button ding) stay audible.

【Strict Prohibitions】

entries.prompt:
THE FINAL WAVE | A DESPERATE TSUNAMI RESCUE

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic live-action cinematic disaster video set in a Japanese coastal fishing village. A massive tsunami approaches after a powerful earthquake. A brave young woman risks her life to rescue stranded people.

CHARACTER & LOCATION:
A young Japanese woman with dark hair in a ponytail, wearing a dark waterproof jacket, black trousers and rubber boots. Three adult fishermen, one small child and one elderly woman. Keep all characters, outfits, faces, rescue boat and village consistent.

EXACT SCENE SEQUENCE:

1. EARTHQUAKE (0–3s):
The village shakes violently. Objects fall, houses rattle and villagers rush outside.

2. TSUNAMI WARNING (3–5s):
Emergency sirens sound. The girl looks towards the ocean as the water suddenly retreats from the harbor.

3. FISHERMEN IN DANGER (5–8s):
She spots three fishermen stranded near a damaged fishing boat, desperately waving for help.

4. RESCUE BOAT (8–11s):
She runs to a small motorboat, unties it and starts the engine.

5. ROUGH SEA (11–15s):
She navigates through violent waves, avoiding floating debris as water splashes over the boat.

6. FISHERMEN RESCUE (15–19s):
She reaches the damaged boat and helps all three fishermen climb safely aboard, catching one as he nearly slips.

7. CHILD AND ELDERLY WOMAN (19–22s):
She spots a frightened child and elderly woman trapped on a flooded rooftop and steers towards them.

8. MASSIVE TSUNAMI (22–26s):
A gigantic dark wave appears behind the harbor. The fishermen help bring the child and elderly woman aboard from a reachable flooded platform.

9. ESCAPE (26–28s):
The boat reaches elevated ground. She helps everyone climb to safety as floodwater crashes through the harbor.

10. FINAL SHOT (28–30s):
The rescued child holds her hand. She watches in shock as the massive wave engulfs the distant village.

VISUAL STYLE:
Ultra-photorealistic live-action disaster film, realistic tsunami physics, powerful water movement, natural handheld documentary camera, stormy daylight, wet clothing, emotional expressions and believable boat movement.

Natural audio: earthquake rumbling, emergency sirens, wind, engine, shouting and crashing waves. No music, subtitles or voiceover.

STRICT CONTINUITY:
Same characters, outfits, boat and location throughout. Show every rescue physically, with logical movement between scenes. No teleportation, superhero powers, cartoon water or unrealistic CGI.

The final video must feel like real disaster footage, full of tension, urgency and emotion.

entries.translated_prompt:
A clear morning on a sandy beach in late autumn. In the shallow water at the surf line, a large whale is stuck and unable to move. A local boy keeps pouring seawater over it with a tin bucket. "I've been pouring water the whole time, but it won't move." Sakura, who is traveling, puts her hand out, but the whale doesn't move at all. "...Living things can't be forced to move." Looking at the sand at his feet, he says, "But if it's the beach itself..."

The sand under the whale cracks in an ellipse, and the mass of sand and seawater lifts into the air. Waves rise up and pool on top of the mass, and the whale spouts. The mass is carried offshore and lowered into the sea, and the whale raises its tail and dives. "Thank you, Sister Sakura!" "Yeah. See you again..." The name he just heard doesn't come to mind. Someone from atop the cliff was watching this.

Recorded by a friend traveling together, handheld camera. No BGM. No added light or aura; only the movement of sand and seawater. Beach, whale, and characters are reference images; the continuation references actual frames from the previous part. Only the opening map and "To be continued" were drawn with code.

entries.title: Palm Beach Aviation Disaster Doc
entries.description: A highly detailed prompt for generating a 2D animated documentary reconstruction of the Palm Beach Learjet crash using Seedance 2.5.
entries.prompt:
PALM BEACH COUNTY, FLORIDA — THE FINAL DESCENT

30-second animated aviation disaster documentary reconstruction | 16:9 horizontal | 2D flat graphic animation | Soft painterly gouache illustration

CREATIVE DIRECTION

Create a sophisticated 2D animated documentary reconstruction of the November 1, 2026 Learjet 60 crash in Palm Beach County, Florida.

Visual language: flat graphic shapes, simplified geometric forms, layered cutout compositions, clean silhouettes, expressive environmental shapes and soft painterly gouache textures.

The animation should resemble a premium illustrated historical documentary, combining editorial graphic design, traditional gouache painting and cinematic 2D motion graphics.

This is NOT 3D animation, NOT photorealism, NOT anime and NOT a children’s cartoon.

Preserve the reported chronology without inventing the accident’s cause. The NTSB investigation is ongoing.

ART DIRECTION

Visual construction:

* Flat 2D geometric shapes.
* Simplified but recognizable aircraft silhouettes.
* Layered foreground, middle-ground and background compositions.
* Hand-painted cloud formations.
* Soft gouache pigment texture across all surfaces.
* Subtle paper grain and imperfect brush edges.
* Clean architectural silhouettes.
* Simplified human figures with believable proportions.
* Controlled shape-based animation and parallax.

Color palette:

* Storm charcoal: #343C43
* Muted blue-grey: #697C87
* Cloud grey: #AEB9B8
* Warm ivory: #E7DFCB
* Concrete beige: #B8A991
* Deep olive: #555B4B
* Emergency burnt orange: #C66B3F
* Smoke brown: #514A43

Use restrained colors, muted contrast and atmospheric depth. Fire should use a limited palette of burnt orange, ochre and deep red rather than exaggerated neon colors.

AIRCRAFT DESIGN

Bombardier Learjet 60, registration N722BD.

Represent the aircraft using accurate recognizable proportions:

* Twin rear-mounted engines.
* Swept wings.
* Pointed nose.
* Conventional vertical tail.
* Slim private business jet fuselage.

Maintain the same aircraft silhouette, proportions, engine placement and registration throughout the sequence.

The aircraft should look like a carefully illustrated Learjet, not a generic passenger plane.

CHRONOLOGICAL STORYBOARD

SHOT 01 — THE FLIGHT | 00:00–00:04

A wide illustrated aerial composition.

A small Learjet 60 travels eastbound above layered South Florida cloud formations.

The aircraft is represented through clean geometric silhouettes with subtle gouache texture.

The camera slowly tracks alongside the jet.

Dark storm formations begin appearing in the distance.

Animation: Slow cloud movement, subtle aircraft movement and gentle parallax between atmospheric layers.

SHOT 02 — ENTERING THE STORM | 00:04–00:08

Cut to a side profile of the Learjet entering increasingly dense grey clouds.

Rain is represented through fine hand-drawn diagonal lines.

Cloud layers overlap the aircraft, gradually reducing visibility.

A simplified cockpit inset shows two pilots monitoring instruments.

The aircraft experiences turbulence, communicated through controlled movement of the aircraft silhouette and subtle cockpit vibration.

Animation: Layered cloud movement, rain streaks and restrained aircraft shaking.

SHOT 03 — EMERGENCY | 00:08–00:12

A graphic transition into a cockpit illustration.

Two pilot silhouettes sit inside the cockpit, surrounded by simplified instrument panels.

A subtle radio-wave graphic appears near the communication equipment to indicate the emergency transmission.

Cut to an exterior view of the Learjet pitching downward through dark cloud layers.

The camera begins following its descent.

No fabricated dialogue or invented technical explanation.

SHOT 04 — THE RAPID DESCENT | 00:12–00:16

A dramatic wide composition showing the aircraft descending through multiple atmospheric layers.

Use layered cloud cutouts moving upward relative to the falling aircraft to communicate extreme vertical speed.

A restrained vertical motion graphic may indicate the direction of descent without displaying invented flight data.

The aircraft banks as it falls.

Camera follows from a distant telephoto perspective.

The composition should communicate danger through scale, speed and visual direction rather than exaggerated effects.

SHOT 05 — IMPACT | 00:16–00:20

Cut to an illustrated ground-level view of Military Trail near 10th Avenue North.

Simplified Palm Beach County buildings, roadside vegetation, electrical infrastructure and road markings establish the location.

The Learjet enters the frame in a steep nose-down descent.

A sudden graphic impact.

The aircraft silhouette disappears into a layered burst of burnt-orange, ochre and charcoal shapes.

Dust, smoke and debris expand outward using controlled 2D shape animation.

No graphic human remains, no exaggerated Hollywood explosion and no lingering destruction spectacle.

SHOT 06 — EMERGENCY RESPONSE | 00:20–00:24

A wide illustrated composition of the crash site.

Fire engines, ambulances and sheriff vehicles arrive along the closed roadway.

Use simplified but recognizable emergency vehicle silhouettes.

A large dark smoke column rises behind the surrounding buildings.

Firefighters approach the perimeter while emergency personnel establish road closures.

Animation: Rotating emergency lights, drifting smoke, subtle vehicle movement and moving silhouettes.

SHOT 07 — COMMUNITY IMPACT | 00:24–00:28

Cut to a nearby residential neighborhood.

Illustrated mobile homes, trees, power infrastructure and residential streets.

Small groups of residents stand outside while emergency personnel assist with evacuation.

Use restrained human silhouettes and natural body language.

The distant smoke column remains visible above the neighborhood.

The scene communicates disruption and community impact without sensationalism.

SHOT 08 — FINAL AFTERMATH | 00:28–00:30

A final wide static composition of the closed crash-site roadway.

Emergency vehicles remain positioned around the perimeter.

A dark smoke column slowly rises into the overcast sky.

The camera gently pulls back.

Fade to a textured charcoal background.

ANIMATION LANGUAGE

Traditional 2D animation with modern editorial motion design.

Use:

* Layered cutout animation.
* Limited frame-by-frame character movement.
* Smooth shape transformations.
* Atmospheric parallax.
* Controlled camera pans and tracking.
* Hand-painted transitions.
* Subtle paper-texture overlays.
* Natural smoke and cloud deformation.

Maintain consistent proportions and shape language between all shots.

Avoid excessive motion graphics, unnecessary typography, decorative transitions and random animated elements.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION

Cinematic illustrated documentary framing.

Wide establishing compositions, side-profile aircraft tracking, distant telephoto perspectives, overhead geographical views and restrained ground-level observation.

Use layered depth to create visual scale despite the flat 2D art style.

Every camera movement must be smooth, deliberate and readable.

No 3D camera rotations, no perspective distortion and no impossible transitions.

SOUND DESIGN

Realistic documentary-inspired audio beneath the illustrated visuals.

Aircraft engine ambience, wind, rain, restrained cockpit radio communication, turbulence-related aircraft sounds, distant impact, fire ambience, sirens and emergency vehicle sounds.

Use subtle orchestral tension that never overwhelms the documentary atmosphere.

Do not fabricate exact ATC recordings or present synthetic dialogue as authentic audio.

CONTINUITY LOCKS

Maintain identical Learjet 60 geometry and aircraft identity across every shot.

Preserve chronological progression from cruise to storm encounter, emergency, uncontrolled descent, impact and response.

Maintain consistent geographical orientation, weather, color palet

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 Feminist Comedy Action Sequence
entries.description: A complex multi-part video prompt for Seedance 2.5 featuring a character named Margo performing martial arts moves in various urban settings, emphasizing realistic physics and continuity.
entries.prompt:
PART 1 — SUBWAY (30s)

Horizontal 16:9, realistic handheld comedy-action. Margo (@Image1), wearing her exact bright pink hooded coat, rides a pink bicycle with her tiny dog in a matching pink hood in the front basket.
00:00–00:11: Cycling through the city, she looks at camera: “My name is Margo. They call me Little Pink Margo. All my life I’ve watched wolves harass women. I’m here to put an end to this [BEEP].”
00:11–00:15: She parks, takes her dog and descends into the subway.
00:15–00:18: Inside (@Image5), a creepy man with enormous bushy eyebrows (@Image3) approaches a young woman (@Image2), leaning too close with puckered lips.
00:18–00:24: Margo performs ONE clear judo hip throw: wrist grip, hip rotation, takeoff, flight and landing. He lands across empty bench seats.
00:24–00:30: Margo sits beside her dog and says: “Wolves are everywhere. Even on the subway. Some just don’t get personal [BEEP] space.” End on her raised eyebrow.

PART 2 — CAFÉ (15s)

Horizontal 16:9, handheld comedy-action. A man (@Image3) refuses to release a waitress's hand (@Image2). Margo watches from a nearby table.
00:00–00:04: She lowers her menu and gives him a cold stare.
00:04–00:08: ONE exaggerated flying kick over the table, striking his chest and tipping him and his chair onto the floor. Clear takeoff, flight and landing.
00:08–00:15: Margo straightens her coat and says: “Kindness isn’t permission. Touch a woman without her consent, and you’ve got a [BEEP] problem. A very pink one.” The waitress is relieved. End on Margo's calm stare.

PART 3 — THE PINK REVOLUTION (30s)

Horizontal 16:9, uplifting handheld street-video. Margo and her dog walk confidently down the street (@Image5). The subway woman (@Image2), waitress (@Image3), office assistant (@Image4) and six more women join her.
00:00–00:07: The subway woman joins Margo.
00:07–00:15: The waitress and assistant join. Margo says: “I’ve spent my whole life fighting these [BEEP] wolves, and I’ll never stop.”
00:15–00:23: Around ten women walk together, smiling and linking arms. Margo says: “No woman should ever feel alone.”
00:23–00:30: Margo faces camera: “Want to join us? Comment I WANT.” She winks. The dog barks once.

VISUAL & SOUND

Natural lighting, realistic skin, handheld camera shake, mild grain, delayed autofocus. Natural city, subway and café sounds. Consistent Margo voice and accurate lip-sync. Classic TV censor beep for every [BEEP]. No music or narrator.

CONTINUITY

Preserve all reference faces, outfits, hair and footwear. Matching pink hoods for Margo and dog. Same characters throughout. Realistic physics, no teleportation, duplication, disappearing people or outfit changes. No cuts during action, subtitles, captions, watermarks or CGI appearance.

entries.title: Seedance 2.5 Floating House Autumn Scene
entries.description: A detailed Japanese prompt for a cinematic scene where a house floats away from a mountain slope, featuring specific camera angles and character actions.
entries.prompt:
晩秋の晴れた朝、山あいの古い家。家のすぐ後ろまで紅葉の山が迫り、坂には重機が滑った溝が残っている。「この家、山に近すぎます」「わたしがいなくなっても、大丈夫なように」。さくらが両腕を伸ばすと、柱の下の礎石が土から抜け、家1軒がまるごと宙に浮き上がる。床の裏から土がこぼれ落ちる。
家は柿の木の上をゆっくり横切り、山から離れた平らな草地へ。途中で傾き、瓦が落ちる。おばあさんが手を上げかける。「おばあちゃんは、使わないで」「力を、抜いて」。家は水平に戻り、草地に着地する。元の場所には四角い土の跡だけが残る。「あそこ、何がありましたっけ」。翌朝、えんじ色の襟巻きを巻いて、さくらは一人で歩いていく。

一緒に来た友達が手持ちで撮った記録。BGMなし。光やオーラは足さず、物が動くだけにした。家・草地・人物は参照画像、続きは前のパートの実際のコマを参照。最後の地図だけコード。
entries.translated_prompt:
On a clear morning in late autumn, an old house nestled in the mountains. A mountain covered in red leaves presses close right behind the house, and there are grooves left by heavy machinery sliding down the slope. "This house is too close to the mountain." "So that I'll be okay even if I disappear." When Sakura stretches both arms out, the foundation stones under the pillars pull free from the earth, and the entire house lifts into the air. Soil falls from beneath the floorboards.
The house slowly crosses over a persimmon tree toward a flat grassy area away from the mountain. It tilts midway, and tiles fall off. The grandmother raises her hand as if to stop it. "Grandma, don't use it." "Let go of the power." The house returns to horizontal and lands on the grass. Only a square patch of bare earth remains where it was. "What was there?" The next morning, wearing a burgundy scarf, Sakura walks alone.

Recorded handheld by a friend who came along. No BGM. No added light or aura; only objects move. The house, grassland, and characters are reference images; continuation references actual frames from previous parts. Only the final map is code.

entries.title: Hollywood Romantic Drama Rooftop Reunion
entries.description: A highly detailed prompt for a 30-second photorealistic romantic drama short film featuring a reunion between two characters on a snowy rooftop terrace, emphasizing cinematic quality and character consistency.
entries.prompt: Create a 30-second photorealistic Hollywood theatrical romantic drama short film. The result must look like a professionally directed and photographed scene from a major Hollywood romantic movie, not an AI-generated montage. FORMAT AND CINEMATOGRAPHY: 30 seconds, 16:9 widescreen, cinematic 2.39:1 composition, authentic 35mm motion-picture film aesthetic, natural organic film grain, anamorphic lens characteristics, realistic shallow depth of field, delicate optical bokeh, natural motion blur, accurate focus transitions and sophisticated cinematic color grading. SETTING: A quiet rooftop terrace overlooking a beautifully illuminated modern city at night. Gentle snowfall, warm practical string lights hanging overhead, a weathered wooden bench, distant apartment windows and subtle rooftop architecture. Cool midnight-blue ambient light contrasts with warm amber practical lighting. Snowfall must look physically realistic and consistent. CHARACTER LOCK — ABSOLUTE: WOMAN: Mid-20s, long naturally wavy dark hair, cream wool coat, deep red knitted scarf, natural makeup and expressive eyes. MAN: Late-20s, short dark hair, charcoal wool overcoat, dark sweater and a subtle layer of snow on his shoulders. Both characters must retain precisely identical facial identities, facial geometry, hairstyles, skin tones, ages, clothing, body proportions and appearance throughout all 30 seconds. No identity drift or character redesign. DIRECTOR'S SCREENPLAY: [00–02s] OPENING HOOK: Hard cut to an extreme macro shot of an old printed photograph resting on a wooden rooftop bench. The photograph shows the same two characters smiling together. A single tear falls onto the photograph as delicate snowflakes land beside it. Authentic paper texture, realistic water interaction and extremely shallow macro focus. A solitary emotional piano note begins. No opening title. [02–04s]: Intimate 85mm close-up of the woman sitting alone beneath warm string lights. She gently holds the photograph with both hands, her thumb moving across its edge. Her eyes are slightly wet. Natural, restrained expression. [04–06s]: Slow lateral dolly movement reveals her sitting alone against the expansive illuminated city skyline. Snow falls naturally through the foreground. Beautiful cinematic depth and realistic environmental detail. [06–08s]: Tight profile close-up. She looks down at the photograph and quietly whispers: "I thought you'd forgotten." A faint metallic rooftop door sound interrupts the silence. She freezes and slowly turns her head. [08–10s]: Over-the-shoulder shot revealing the rooftop entrance opening. The man stands in the doorway, breathing naturally after climbing the stairs. His charcoal coat carries a thin layer of snow. Warm interior light outlines his silhouette. [10–12s]: Intimate close-up of the woman's face as she recognizes him. Her eyes widen slightly, her lips part, and disbelief slowly becomes relief. Avoid exaggerated crying or artificial facial expressions. [12–14s]: Medium close-up of the man taking one hesitant step forward. He looks directly at her and softly says: "I never stopped coming back to you." [14–17s] THE REUNION: She rises and quickly crosses the distance between them, wrapping both arms around him. He instinctively embraces her, holding her firmly but naturally. Use subtle handheld camera movement to follow the action. Snowflakes pass through the warm string lights. Their body movements and physical contact must be anatomically accurate. [17–19s]: Intimate close-up over his shoulder. Her fingers grip the back of his charcoal coat. She closes her eyes and finally allows herself to cry. He gently rests his cheek against her hair. Genuine emotional performance, natural breathing and realistic fabric movement. [19–21s]: Side-profile medium close-up. They slowly pull apart while keeping their hands together. She looks into his eyes and softly says: "You took your time." [21–22s]: Close-up of the man. A small, genuine smile appears. He answers quietly: "I know." [22–25s] THE KISS: He gently brushes a loose strand of hair away from her face. They move closer and share a tender, natural kiss. No exaggerated movement or artificial posing. Snow falls through the amber practical lighting. Beautiful optical depth and subtle cinematic motion. [25–28s] CINEMATIC FINALE: A smooth, carefully controlled crane movement pulls away and upward, revealing the couple embracing beneath the rooftop string lights. The illuminated city stretches behind them. Their silhouettes remain naturally integrated into the environment. The piano and strings reach a gentle emotional resolution. [28–30s] FINAL IMAGE: Cut to the old photograph resting on the wooden bench in the foreground. A controlled rack focus reveals the reunited couple embracing softly in the background. Elegant, understated gold serif typography fades in: "A LOVE THAT WAITED" Smaller line: "Some promises outlive time." Hold briefly and cut to black. SOUND DESIGN: Original emotional piano and restrained orchestral strings from the first frame. Natural rooftop wind, distant city ambience, gentle snowfall, realistic rooftop door creak, footsteps, clothing movement, intimate breathing and authentic dialogue. Music builds gradually during the reunion, swells gently during the kiss and resolves warmly at the ending. No generic trailer booms, artificial whooshes or excessive sound effects. LIGHTING AND COLOR: Warm practical tungsten illumination against cool midnight-blue ambient light. Natural skin tones, realistic shadow falloff, subtle highlights, controlled contrast and organic film texture. Avoid oversaturated orange-and-blue grading. PERFORMANCE DIRECTION: Both actors must behave like real people in an emotionally intimate film. Subtle eye movements, authentic hesitation, natural dialogue delivery, believable breathing and realistic physical interaction. No theatrical crying, exaggerated smiles or artificial gestures. STRICT NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS: No AI-generated appearance, no plastic skin, no beauty filters, no facial morphing, no identity drift, no duplicated characters, no extra fingers, no malformed hands, no distorted faces, no inconsistent wardrobe, no changing hairstyles, no floating objects, no artificial snow effects, no random background changes, no video-game aesthetics, no excessive lens flares, no unnecessary transitions, no artificial camera movements, no overprocessed HDR, no subtitles, no captions or unnecessary text. FINAL QUALITY TARGET: An emotionally memorable, visually sophisticated Hollywood romantic drama with exceptional facial consistency, authentic human performances, realistic environmental physics, professional cinematography and a powerful final emotional payoff. Every shot must belong to the same film, the same location and the same continuous moment.

entries.title: Autumn Street Walk Sequence

entries.prompt:
Create a 30-second ultra-realistic 16:9 landscape video featuring the same naturally attractive 24-year-old Korean woman  with long loose dark hair, minimal natural makeup, an oversized black knitted sweater, loose casual pants, and a soft knitted scarf. Preserve her exact facial identity, hairstyle, outfit, scarf, and body proportions throughout the entire video.

The setting is a charming, peaceful Seoul residential neighborhood during a beautiful autumn afternoon. Small Korean shops, narrow sidewalks, cozy cafés, street vendors, scattered golden leaves, and warm sunlight create a nostalgic everyday atmosphere.

Shot 1 — 0–7 seconds: The Balloon Surprise

She walks casually along a neighborhood sidewalk, enjoying the afternoon. A small street vendor nearby is holding a bunch of colorful helium balloons. Suddenly, a few balloons slip away and float gently into the air. One colorful balloon drifts towards her. She notices it, reaches up, catches its ribbon, and smiles with genuine surprise. She continues walking and notices a couple of children playing with giant soap bubbles outside a small neighborhood shop. entries.prompt:
[Style + Camera + Atmosphere]

A man sitting in a car parked on the shore of an icy lake, filmed with raw handheld phone video realism. He holds the phone behind the windshield, about 400 meters away from people on the ice. One continuous 30-second shot, no cuts. The phone stays inside the car throughout. Anxious amateur zooming throughout: constant small pinch-zoom adjustments, in and out a bit, closer, then back, then closer again, overshoot and correct, each zoom becomes softer, noisier, more blocky, focus hunting on glass, handheld panning following action. Flat gray winter daylight, cold blue tones, compressed phone quality, unedited upload. Thin smoke rising from the grill on the parked pickup drifts throughout.

[Image References]

{{Mixed 1}} is the first frame: video starts exactly here.
{{Mixed 2}} is the man's character view, do not change facial features. Ignore its background.
{{Mixed 3}} is the woman: face. Do not change facial features, ignore its background.

[Cast + Props — Locked]

One man, one woman, one black cat, one fish, one beer can, one net. Man only holds a short ice fishing rod until she hands him the can. Pickup truck parked to their right.

[Timeline]

0-3s: Exactly [image_1_initial_frame]. Phone suddenly zooms in slightly on the tiny group, then backs off, then pushes in.
3-7s: Soft and grainy, small zoom corrections. Woman on left back to camera, taking a cold beer can from red cooler. Man in center calmly sitting on folding chair, fishing through hole in ice.
7-10s: She opens can, walks over to hand it to him. Holding rod with one hand, he takes can with other. Phone pulls back one notch, then pushes in.
10-13s: He slowly sips. Rod tip bends and twitches. Phone suddenly zooms close to rod.
13-18s: He drops can, beer foams on ice, grabs rod with two hands, stands up pulling hard. Woman grabs net, kneels by hole. Medium-sized fish thrashing up on line. She shouts {Yoo-hoo!}, he nods. Phone pulls back one notch to fit both.

21-24s: Cat jumps down to ice, right next to man, swipes hanging fish off line with paw, grabs it in mouth, darts right. Woman's net swings empty.
24-27s: Man drops rod, chases cat right, boots slipping. Phone pans right following and pulls back; cat exits frame right. White cracks spread under his feet.
27-30s: Ice breaks, he plunges into water, pops up grabbing edge, beanie floating. Woman holds head with hands. Phone zooms to him, guy filming shouts {What the fuck!}

[Audio]

Everything on ice is distant: faint, muffled through closed windshield, under car hum and wind noise, even when image zooms. Woman's shout and splash sounds small and distant. Only filming guy's voice sounds near. Language: American English. No music. No subtitles.

Hard cut to a beautifully composed, steady frontal shot of her standing on a Warsaw sidewalk. Begin framed from the waist up, with softly defocused café terraces, pedestrians, and urban architecture behind her.

Continuity: Strict facial identity, clothing, hairstyle, and accessory consistency. Coffee appears after the café scene; the book appears after the bookstore scene. Natural human movement, believable object handling, and no duplicated or disappearing props.

Performance: Relaxed, expressive but understated. Brief natural eye contact, subtle smiles, and believable conversational body language. No exaggerated acting, unnecessary gestures, or invented interactions.

At 11:59 PM, a young Korean man stands alone on a deserted railway platform during heavy rain. The station announcement suddenly stops mid-sentence. A distant train headlight appears inside a dark tunnel, even though the electronic display says the last train departed hours ago.

Cut to black.

LIGHTING: Cold blue station lighting, warm vintage light inside the train, realistic shadows, subtle fog, wet reflective surfaces, and cinematic Korean noir color grading.

entries.title: Zombie Apocalypse Action Sequence
entries.description: A detailed prompt for a 30-second horizontal zombie apocalypse action sequence featuring a female protagonist with specific attire fighting in Manhattan.
entries.prompt:
FORMAT
30 seconds. Horizontal 16:9. Photorealistic live-action sequence from a big-budget zombie apocalypse action film. Relentless forward momentum, extremely fast attackers, explosive superhuman combat, readable choreography. Everything plays at full real-time speed. No slow motion, speed ramps or introductory establishing shot.

REFERENCE
Reference image 1: the uploaded full-body photograph of the adult female protagonist. Preserve her exact face, body proportions, short pink-to-purple-to-blue hair, hair clips, pink-and-white cropped top, matching pleated skirt, pink backpack and heavy black boots with pink platform soles, straps and metal details. Keep her identity and outfit consistent in every shot. Her backpack remains secured over both shoulders.

The reference defines her appearance only. Replace the neutral background with the location below.

VISUAL REALISM
Convincing live-action cinematography with natural skin texture, sweat, dust, individual hair strands, detailed fabric and worn materials. Photorealistic visual effects integrated into real-looking street photography.

Her strength and jumping ability are supernatural. Everything affected by her strength retains convincing mass, inertia, gravity and material behavior. Her movements look controlled and almost effortless; the resulting collisions are violent and heavy.

Metal buckles locally before the vehicle shifts. Glass fractures and scatters. Brickwork breaks at the impact point, releasing individual bricks and powder. Bodies follow continuous ballistic trajectories and land with weight. No weightless floating, rubbery bodies, glowing powers or visible energy waves.

LOCATION AND SPATIAL LAYOUT
Post-apocalyptic Midtown Manhattan, on a fictional block near West 38th Street and Eighth Avenue. Recognizable New York architecture: tall weathered buildings, brick storefronts, exterior fire escapes, rooftop water towers, faded street signs, traffic lights and a subway entrance behind bent railings.

Cold overcast late-afternoon light. Smoke hangs between buildings. Damp asphalt, shallow puddles, scattered paper, broken glass and abandoned yellow taxis. Dead shop windows, rusting shutters and vegetation pushing through pavement cracks. Distant fires provide small warm accents without overwhelming the natural daylight.

Maintain one coherent street throughout:
- The heroine initially runs north through a clear lane.
- The main pursuing horde follows from the south.
- A damaged yellow taxi stands beside the west curb near the opening action.
- Farther north, a stalled dark coupe provides the platform for her jump.
- A second group approaches from a narrow passage between buildings on the east side.
- Beside that passage is a thin, weathered brick storefront infill wall. This is the wall broken during combat, not a massive structural building column.
- A separate abandoned silver sedan stands farther north, roughly parallel to the east curb.
- Across from this sedan, a cracked concrete construction barrier borders the west side.
- A delivery van stands farther south along the west side, behind the later car collision.
- The east edge of the street retains a narrow open route around the displaced sedan.

Introduce relevant objects in the background before they become part of the action. Do not rearrange the street between shots.

CHARACTERS AND PERFORMANCE
The heroine is an adult woman with extraordinary physical strength, acceleration, balance and durability. Focused eyes, calm determination, no frightened hesitation, posing or celebratory pauses. Her gaze tracks each immediate threat before she commits to a movement.

Her boots make firm contact with the ground. Her knees absorb landings. Her hips and shoulders drive strikes. Hair, skirt and backpack respond naturally to acceleration, braking and rotation.

The zombies are adult infected people in filthy, damaged everyday New York clothing. Pale mottled skin, exhausted faces, frantic eyes and aggressive expressions. They sprint at extreme speed with forceful leg drive and irregular but anatomically believable strides. They leap across obstacles, scramble over cars and collide when their paths become blocked.

They continuously pursue visible routes toward her. They do not wait politely for their turn. Use cars, the narrow passage and fallen attackers to stagger their arrival naturally. Keep the violence focused on impacts and environmental destruction rather than explicit gore.

TIMELINE AND CHOREOGRAPHY

00:00-00:05 | SPRINT AND FIRST IMPACT
Begin already in motion.

A low front three-quarter tracking camera retreats at the heroine's running speed. She sprints north between abandoned vehicles, leaning slightly forward, arms pumping close to her body, boots striking damp pavement and kicking droplets backward.

Behind her, the main horde pours through the gaps between cars. The leading infected man closes the distance and launches forward, reaching toward her shoulders.

She glances over her left shoulder and sees him commit to the leap. She shortens her stride, plants her left foot, pivots toward him and brings her right fist close to her ribs. As he enters reach, she rotates her hips and drives one compact right punch into the center of his chest.

Show the fist making contact. His torso folds around the impact for an instant, then his whole body is driven diagonally backward toward the west curb.

The camera tracks laterally enough to hold her follow-through and his flight in the same readable composition. He slams back-first into the side of the yellow taxi. Its doors buckle inward, a side window bursts and the car jolts sideways on its suspension. He drops beside the crushed doors and remains there.

She retracts her fist, pivots north again and immediately resumes running. The other pursuers continue closing through the available lane.

00:05-00:10 | RUNNING VAULT OVER THE SECOND GROUP
Cut on her running movement to a side tracking view.

The second group bursts out of the east-side passage ahead and turns into her path. The heroine takes two rapid approach steps toward the stalled dark coupe. She plants one boot on the hood near its reinforced edge, depressing the metal, then forcefully extends that leg to launch forward and upward.

She clears the first two attackers in one powerful forward jump. Her knees draw upward just enough to clear their reaching hands; her arms balance her rotation. No somersault and no hovering.

The camera follows her full arc in a medium-wide profile. The attackers rush underneath her, overshoot and begin turning back.

She lands beyond them on an already visible clear patch of asphalt, right foot followed immediately by left, knees flexing to absorb the impact. Dust and water kick outward from her soles. Her backpack swings forward against its straps, then settles back.

She uses a short braking step to turn south toward the attackers. Show the landing before the next cut. The main horde is still approaching from farther south, temporarily slowed by the congested vehicle gaps.

00:10-00:16 | WALL STRIKE AND BODY THROW
A moving medium-wide three-quarter shot keeps her full body, the nearest attackers and the brick storefront visible.

The nearest zombie finishes turning and lunges at her with both hands. She shifts half a step outside his reaching arms, bends her knees slightly, draws her right elbow back and rotates through one rising punch into his upper abdomen.

Show a single clear contact. Her fist travels upward and diagonally toward the east-side storefront. The attacker lifts off his feet and is propelled backward into the thin brick infill wall.

His upper back strikes first. The wall collapses inward around the contact area. Bricks tumble into the dark shop interior and onto the pavement

晩秋の晴れた昼、山あいの古い家。干し柿を取り込むさくらたちの裏山で、無人の黄色いショベルカーが坂を滑り落ちてくる。切り株に乗り上げて、車体が傾いて止まる。運転席は空。「誰も、乗っとらん」。切り株に裂け目が走る。さくらの顔が固まる。「わたしが、やります」「ひとつ、消えるよ」。切り株が裂け、重機がまた滑り出す。

さくらが腕を伸ばす。重機は鈍るが、押し返される。軒下の干し柿の向こうで、車体が大きくなっていく。おばあさんがさくらの肩をたたく。「力を、抜いて」。さくらが長く息を吐く。キャタピラが地面から離れ、巨大な車体が空へ上がる。2人の顔に影が落ちる。重機は軒先の手前に下りる。坂に2本の深い溝が残る。作業の人が走ってくる。「止まってましたよ」。縁側で、先生が干し柿を渡す。

一緒に来た友達が手持ちで撮った記録。1カット2秒前後、BGMなし。重機は1台、運転席はずっと空。光やオーラは足さず、物が動くだけにした。坂・重機・干し柿は参照画像、続きは前のパートの実際のコマを参照にした。
entries.translated_prompt:
A sunny day in late autumn, an old house in the mountains. On the back hill where Sakura and others are drying persimmons, an unmanned yellow excavator slides down the slope. It hits a tree stump, tilts, and stops. The driver's seat is empty. "No one is riding it." A crack runs through the stump. Sakura's face freezes. "I'll do it." "One will disappear." The stump splits, and the heavy machinery starts sliding again.

Sakura extends her arm. The excavator slows but is pushed back. Behind the dried persimmons under the eaves, the vehicle body grows larger. Grandma taps Sakura's shoulder. "Let go of your strength." Sakura exhales deeply. The caterpillar tracks lift off the ground, and the huge vehicle body rises into the air. Shadows fall on their faces. The excavator lands just before the eaves. Two deep grooves remain on the slope. Workers run over. "It stopped." On the veranda, the teacher hands over dried persimmons.

Recorded handheld by a friend who came along. About 2 seconds per cut, no BGM. One excavator, driver's seat always empty. No light or aura added, just objects moving. Slope, excavator, and persimmons are reference images; continuation refers to actual frames from previous parts.
